title: Termwise monoidal functors preserve the signed total tensor constraints
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with monoidal structures [def-sfb-monoidal-category] whose tensors are additive in each variable. Assume all small colimits exist and tensoring on either side preserves them [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. On integer-indexed cochain complexes use the signed direct-sum total tensor [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso] and its monoidal constraints [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy]. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be additive, preserve countable coproducts, and have a specified strong monoidal structure [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor], with inverse tensorator $c_{A,B}:F(A\otimes B)\cong FA\otimes FB$ and unit $e_F:\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}\cong F\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}$. Write $F_{\rm Ch}$ for termwise application of $F$, $I_{\mathcal C}=\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}[0]$, and $I_{\mathcal D}=\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}[0]$.
There are natural isomorphisms $\tau_{P,Q}:F_{\rm Ch}(P\otimes Q)\cong F_{\rm Ch}P\otimes F_{\rm Ch}Q$ uniquely specified on each bidegree summand by
$$\tau_{P,Q}^n\circ F(\iota_{p,q})=\iota'_{p,q}\circ c_{P^p,Q^q}\qquad(p+q=n).$$
Let $j:F_{\rm Ch}I_{\mathcal C}\cong I_{\mathcal D}$ be $e_F^{-1}$ in degree zero, with the canonical zero-object identifications in other degrees. For all unbounded complexes $P,Q,R$, the ordinary complex associator and unitors satisfy
$$(1\otimes\tau_{Q,R})\circ\tau_{P,Q\otimes R}\circ F_{\rm Ch}(\alpha_{P,Q,R})=\alpha_{FP,FQ,FR}\circ(\tau_{P,Q}\otimes1)\circ\tau_{P\otimes Q,R},$$
$$F_{\rm Ch}(\lambda_P)=\lambda_{FP}\circ(j\otimes1)\circ\tau_{I_{\mathcal C},P},\qquad F_{\rm Ch}(\rho_P)=\rho_{FP}\circ(1\otimes j)\circ\tau_{P,I_{\mathcal C}}.$$
In particular $\tau^{-1},j^{-1}$ give a strong monoidal structure on $F_{\rm Ch}$. No symmetry compatibility of $F$ is required.

proof.text: For fixed $n$, the index set $S_n=\{(p,q)\in\mathbf Z^2:p+q=n\}$ is countable, by the bijection $p\mapsto(p,n-p)$. Since $F$ preserves this coproduct, the maps $F(\iota_{p,q})$ make $F((P\otimes Q)^n)$ a coproduct of the objects $F(P^p\otimes Q^q)$. By the universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], there is a unique $\tau^n$ with $\tau^nF(\iota_{p,q})=\iota'_{p,q}c_{P^p,Q^q}$. Define $\sigma^n$ out of the target coproduct by $\sigma^n\iota'_{p,q}=F(\iota_{p,q})c_{P^p,Q^q}^{-1}$. Composing these equations and using $cc^{-1}=1$ gives $\sigma^n\tau^n=1$ and $\tau^n\sigma^n=1$, since maps out of either coproduct are determined by their composites with the injections.

proof.text:
Write $A=P^p$, $B=Q^q$. On $F(P^p\otimes Q^q)$ the two composites $d_{FP\otimes FQ}\tau^n$ and $\tau^{n+1}F(d_{P\otimes Q})$ are both
$$\iota'_{p+1,q}(F(d_P^p)\otimes1)c_{A,B}+(-1)^p\iota'_{p,q+1}(1\otimes F(d_Q^q))c_{A,B}.$$
Indeed substitute the two summand terms of the differential in [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso], use $F(u+v)=F(u)+F(v)$ and $F(-u)=-F(u)$, and use naturality of $c=\mu^{-1}$ from [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] separately with $(d_P^p,1)$ and $(1,d_Q^q)$. The preserved-coproduct uniqueness of step 1 proves the chain equation. Its degreewise inverse $\sigma$ is a chain map too: multiply that chain equation on the two sides by $\sigma^{n+1}$ and $\sigma^n$. Thus $\tau$ is an isomorphism of complexes.

proof.text:
For cochain maps $a:P\to P'$ and $b:Q\to Q'$, test naturality on $F(\iota_{p,q})$. The two resulting maps are
$$\iota''_{p,q}(F(a^p)\otimes F(b^q))c_{P^p,Q^q},\qquad\iota''_{p,q}c_{P'^p,Q'^q}F(a^p\otimes b^q).$$
They agree by tensorator naturality in [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor], after taking the inverse tensorator. The summand formula for $a\otimes b$ is part of [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. The coproduct universal property therefore proves naturality in both variables and uniqueness of the stated natural complex isomorphism.

proof.text: An additive functor sends a zero object to a zero object: $1_{F0}=F(1_0)=F(0)=0$, and an object whose identity is zero has exactly one arrow to and from every object. Thus $F_{\rm Ch}(\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}[0])$ has $F\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}$ in degree zero and zero objects elsewhere. Its differentials vanish. The map $e_F^{-1}$ in degree zero and the unique zero-object isomorphisms elsewhere form the required chain isomorphism $j$, whose inverse is $e_F$ in degree zero. This uses the zero object supplied by [def-sp-abelian] and the given unit isomorphism of [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor].

proof.text:
Use [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy]: the complex associators are induced by the coefficient associator and the reindexing $(p+q)+r=p+(q+r)$. Tensor preservation of coproducts and the universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] show that the nested triple inclusions determine maps out of $((P\otimes Q)\otimes R)^n$. Applying $F$ keeps this property: both nested indices are countable, so its assumed coproduct preservation applies twice. Precompose the proposed associativity equation with $F$ of such an inclusion, with $p+q+r=n$. Put $A=P^p,B=Q^q,C=R^r$. Naturality of $c$ moves the inner summand inclusions past the outer $c$. After the common final triple inclusion, the two coefficient maps are
$$(1\otimes c_{B,C})c_{A,B\otimes C}F(\alpha_{A,B,C}),\qquad\alpha_{FA,FB,FC}(c_{A,B}\otimes1)c_{A\otimes B,C}.$$
These agree: substitute $c=\mu^{-1}$ in the associativity identity of [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] and cancel the invertible tensorators. This proves the equation in every degree. No permutation of factors occurred, hence there is no Koszul sign or symmetry hypothesis in this check.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ, lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes, proof: associator coherence; functor equation expanded using the coefficient tensorator (agent verification).

proof.text:
For the left unit equation, the only potentially nonzero summand of $(I_{\mathcal C}\otimes P)^n$ is $(0,n)$; for the right unit equation, that of $(P\otimes I_{\mathcal C})^n$ is $(n,0)$. All other summands have a zero factor: additivity of tensor gives $1_{0\otimes A}=0\otimes1_A=0$ and similarly for $A\otimes0$. By [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy], the complex unitors on the surviving summands are the coefficient unitors. By steps 1 and 4, the claimed equations there become, for $A=P^n$,
$$F(\lambda_A)=\lambda_{FA}(e_F^{-1}\otimes1)c_{\mathbf1,A},\qquad F(\rho_A)=\rho_{FA}(1\otimes e_F^{-1})c_{A,\mathbf1}.$$
They follow by cancelling $\mu_{\mathbf1,A}(e_F\otimes1)$ and $\mu_{A,\mathbf1}(1\otimes e_F)$ respectively from the two unit identities in [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. On the zero summands both sides are the unique map. Coproduct uniqueness proves both full complex equations.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ, lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes, proof: left and right unitors; coefficient unit identities after restriction to degrees (0,n) and (n,0) (agent verification).

proof.text: Set $\mu^{\rm Ch}_{P,Q}=\tau_{P,Q}^{-1}$ and $e^{\rm Ch}=j^{-1}$. Step 3 gives the naturality of $\mu^{\rm Ch}$. Substitute these inverses into the identities proved in steps 5 and 6 and compose with the invertible $\tau$ and $j$ to cancel them. The resulting three identities are exactly the associativity, left unit and right unit identities in [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor], for the complex monoidal structures of [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy]. They therefore give the stated strong monoidal structure on $F_{\rm Ch}$.
